R638.note: Host allowlist plus rejection of non-relative schemes closes the redirect; relative paths still work and the host restriction is the fix itself, not extra narrowing.

R639.note: Placeholder plus DB::select($sql, [$region]) binding; query shape, result type and response unchanged.

R640.note: vector<string_view> to vector<string> gives the cache ownership; remember/firstLetter semantics and the out-of-range concern are left exactly as the contract asks.

R641.note: toRealPath on base and resolved path with Path.startsWith containment; 404-on-missing preserved, and the added leading-slash rejection is something the containment check would refuse anyway.

R642.note: Parameterized JNDI filter (cn={0}) with filterArgs; the added new SearchControls() is what the API documents null as meaning, so search scope and limits are unchanged.

R643.note: Static SecureRandom with 16 random bytes, url-safe base64; only the token's format changes, which is the point of the fix, and cookie/session handling is untouched.

R644.note: check_password() is the right API, but the stored column holds 2019-migration plaintext, so every existing legacy user is locked out (unparseable hash yields False, or ValueError on older Django) while the write-up claims the opposite - 'compatible with legacy data' - so the break is not disclosed.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read is the right source and the 32-char key, alphabet, map write and 400 path are preserved; the byte%36 mapping carries a small modulo bias (256 = 7*36+4) that is not material at 32 characters.

R646.note: jwt.verify with a string secret restricts to HS algorithms and closes the forge, but next() is called inside the try, so a synchronous downstream error is swallowed and rewritten as a 401 'Invalid or expired token' instead of reaching Express's error handler - unstated.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with setString(1, data) and no-arg executeQuery; resource close chain and logging preserved verbatim.

R648.note: %q escapes CR/LF and non-printables (including U+2028) via strconv.Quote, so the forged-entry vector is closed; the only change is the now-quoted log field, stated plainly.

R649.note: Moving the write after login_user matches the flagged ordering but is effectively a no-op: Flask-Login 0.6.3 login_user only adds keys and never clears the cookie session, so an attacker-planted pre-login session still survives - no session.clear() before establishing the login.

R650.note: The array form fixes the Unix branch, but the Windows branch still routes through cmd.exe /c and Java only quotes args containing space/tab/</> for a .exe, so a metacharacter with no space (e.g. x&whoami) is still parsed by cmd; separately the absolute SYSTEM32 path to cmd.exe was silently changed to a PATH-resolved cmd.exe and data is no longer whitespace-split into multiple operands.

R651.note: libmagic content sniffing plus a server-generated uuid name closes the dangerous-type upload, but the three-entry MIME allowlist rejects the other document types the endpoint's own docstring advertises ('PDF, DOCX, etc.') and the response now returns a generated filename instead of the submitted one - both disclosed, so a legitimate caller is still turned away.
